title: First and mean flight dates gave opposite average species order in four England and Wales butterfly samples, 1985-2024
abstract: We tested whether May-June warmth changed the mean flight-date gap between Ringlet and Meadow Brown at the same sites. We used 14,504 paired site-years at 881 public UK monitoring sites in England and Wales in 1985-2004 and 2005-2024. Four models controlled site, time and rain. All four corrected temperature intervals included zero. We then found an unplanned descriptive result: average first Ringlet dates were 6.9-9.7 days later than Meadow Brown dates, but average mean Ringlet flight dates were 7.9-12.6 days earlier. This average order reversal remained in high-count and common-site checks. Strict reversals occurred in 45-56 percent of weighted site-year pairs. Meadow Brown had a wider recorded flight period. This can explain the metric difference, but visits, activity and detection can also affect it. These data do not establish a common warmth effect on the gap, a species interaction, or a causal climate effect. Few early Welsh sites, common regional weather, missing visits, selected paired records and country weather limit inference. The package gives exact source snapshots and hashes, code, all results, figures and independent numerical checks.
